title: How RSI14 behaves around the 40 and 60 lines (hold / break / range) on 1h/4h/12h/1d, cushion, context, bounce vs wait plays, BTCUSDT+ETHUSDT SPOT 2017-08..2025-06

what.name: Event
what.value_plain: RSI14 enters the band [L-c, L+c] around line 40 or 60 from above or from below, on 1h/4h/12h/1d; cushion c in {1,2,3,5} RSI points; outcome window N = 24/18/14/10 bars
what.label: OURS

what.name: Outcome
what.value_plain: HOLD = leaves the band on the side it came from; BREAK = closes beyond the line by more than c on the far side; RANGE = crossed the line twice or more before leaving, or stayed inside N bars
what.label: OURS

what.name: Plays
what.value_plain: take the bounce (enter at the HOLD confirmation, direction RSI left the band) vs wait for the break (enter at the BREAK confirmation); entry next bar open, exit N bars later
what.label: OURS

what.name: Context
what.value_plain: higher-TF RSI vs 50, number of other TFs at the same line (0-3), regime (Malkan weekly+monthly 60/40 with SMA200 side) and SMA200-side-age phase (fresh <= 60 daily closes)
what.label: OURS

what.name: Power gate
what.value_plain: prereg_gate m = 6: all 64 event cells BLOCK (event days 65-2015), so every play cell is capped INCONCLUSIVE
what.label: OURS

what.name: Spot vs futures caveat
what.value_plain: spot not futures; 2 symbols; 2022-24 half of DEV overlaps the sibling long-window studies; archive gaps not filled
what.label: OURS

how: PRE_REG.md frozen first (commit 022511723); cushion and plays picked on DEV only; VALIDATION 2024-07..2025-06 read once on the 6 picked play cells; Holm m = 6; day-clustered 95 % CI; DEFAULT needs power PASS and fee-net CI above 0. A random-walk benchmark (same rules, 200 000 synthetic bars per timeframe) sits beside every base rate.
window: DEV 2017-08..2024-06, VALIDATION 2024-07..2025-06 (picks only), HOLDOUT never loaded; BTCUSDT+ETHUSDT SPOT klines, 12h built from 1h, no futures splice

verdict.label: NO DEFAULT PLAY. RSI14 at the 40 and 60 lines behaves close to a random-walk benchmark (hold +1.5 points, break -1.7 points over chance, averaged over 16 timeframe x line x side cells; range 21-33 %); the cushion that best separates hold from break is mostly geometry (c=5 on the side RSI came from, c=1 on the other). Another timeframe at the same line raises the hold rate (+7 to +18 points); an aligned higher-timeframe bias lowers it (-10 to -14 points on 1h-12h). Both plays (take the bounce, wait for the break) are INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered, not FAIL): the power gate (m = 6) blocks all 64 event cells, the 6 DEV picks keep 2-9 events each on VALIDATION. HOLDOUT never loaded.

why: Base rates: at the picked cushion hold is 25-58 %, break 15-51 %, range 21-33 % depending on timeframe and side; the random-walk benchmark gives nearly the same split (hold +1.5, break -1.7 points on average); 1h/4h cells show the largest real excess (+4.4 to +6.7 points of hold).

What changes the odds: another timeframe's RSI inside the same band raises hold (+7.0 [5.3, 8.7] on 1h, +12.4 on 4h, +18.4 on 12h, +17.0 on 1d); a higher-TF bias that agrees with the bounce lowers it (-10.0 on 1h, -12.3 on 4h, -14.2 on 12h; 1d -2.0 spans 0). Regime (bull vs range) and phase (fresh vs mature) move hold by at most 1.3 points on 1h-12h; the bear regime never occurs.

Plays: 15 of 214 eligible DEV play cells have a fee-net CI above 0 (7 %, chance about 5 %); the 6 picks keep 2-9 events on VALIDATION with CIs spanning 0; unfiltered mean fee-net per cell bounce +0.005 %, wait +0.028 %. All INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered).
Next step: a larger-universe study of 'another timeframe at the same line' (confluence), the one factor with a consistent hold-rate effect; each a new PRE_REG.
